nodeData.note: The whole system: levels, competencies, values, assessment.

children.note: Kenya's Competency Based Curriculum (CBC) is the school system from nursery to Grade 12. It aims for children who can use what they learn, not only remember it. This map shows the big picture: the levels, the skills and values, assessment, and the part parents play.

nodeData.note: Kenya's Competency Based Curriculum (CBC) is the school system from nursery to Grade 12. It aims for children who can use what they learn, not only remember it. This map shows the big picture: the levels, the skills and values, assessment, and the part parents play.

children.note: In plain words: school should help children DO things with what they learn. Knowing facts still matters, but using them is the goal.

children.topic: Able to use what you learn
children.note: KICD describes a competency as being able to use the right knowledge, skills, attitudes and values to do a task well. Example: measuring and pricing items at the market, not just reciting a times table.

manas.q: What is a competency, in plain words?

children.note: Lessons are meant to be hands-on: experiments, projects, group work and real tasks, so children learn through experience.
The framework puts the child, their needs, talents and interests at the heart of learning, rather than the syllabus alone.
Teachers plan learning activities that suit each child, then guide and observe, instead of only lecturing.
CBC was launched in 2017 and phased in grade by grade. You may also hear it called CBE (Competency Based Education).

manas.q: In which year was CBC launched in Kenya?

children.note: 8-4-4 was the system CBC is replacing. Here is a neutral side-by-side of the main ideas, not a judgement of either.
Eight years of primary, four of secondary and four of university, introduced in 1985.

manas.q: What did the numbers in 8-4-4 stand for?

children.note: The 2019 framework notes concerns that 8-4-4 was heavy on content and exams, with limited practical skills.
CBC aims to cover less content in depth and focus on applying knowledge in real life.
8-4-4 relied mostly on final exams. CBC aims to balance ongoing classroom checks with end-of-level assessments.
CBC has 2 years pre-primary, 6 primary, 3 junior school and 3 senior school before college or university.

manas.q: What is the CBC structure in years?

children.note: From nursery to Grade 12, CBC has four main stages. Each stage has its own map in this library.
Two years of nursery before Grade 1. Learning is mostly through play, songs and stories.

manas.q: How many years is pre-primary in CBC?

children.note: Children build reading, writing and number skills. Grade 1 starts at about age 6.

manas.q: At about what age does a child start Grade 1?

children.note: Learning areas become more like subjects, such as Science and Technology and Social Studies.
Three years of junior school (junior secondary), with areas such as Integrated Science and Pre-Technical Studies.

manas.q: Which grades make up junior school?

children.note: Three years where learners follow a pathway that matches their interests. KICD's framework gives the age as about 16–18.

manas.q: Which grades make up senior school?

children.note: Official papers group levels: Early Years = pre-primary plus lower primary; Middle School = upper primary plus junior school.

manas.q: Which levels make up 'Early Years Education'?

children.note: Seven big skills every learner builds in every learning area, from PP1 to Grade 12. One bubble each, with an everyday example.
Speaking, listening, writing and working well with others. Example: siblings planning together how to share the chores.

manas.q: Name the core competency about talking and working with others.

children.note: Believing in yourself and your ability to manage tasks. Example: a child who tries again after a sum goes wrong, and gets it right.
Thinking things through and finding solutions. Example: working out why the tomato seedlings are wilting and what to change.

manas.q: Which core competency is about reasoning and finding solutions?

children.note: Making new things and ideas. Example: building a toy lorry from a carton and bottle tops.
Caring for your community and country. Example: helping clean the estate or school compound.
Using phones, computers and the internet safely and well. Example: looking up the weather with a parent and talking about safe use.

manas.q: Which core competency covers using technology safely?

children.note: Knowing how to keep learning on your own. Example: a child who looks up a new word, notes it and uses it later.
Values CBC aims to nurture, drawn from Kenya's Constitution (2019 framework). Parents are the first teachers of values; children learn them mostly by example.
Doing your part. Example: feeding the chickens every morning without being reminded.
Treating people and things well. Example: greeting elders and waiting your turn to speak.
Doing your best work. Example: rewriting homework neatly because you care about it.
Helping others who are in need. Example: checking on a sick neighbour or a classmate who is sad.
Accepting people who differ from us. Example: making friends with a classmate from another community or faith.
Telling the truth and keeping promises. Example: returning extra change to the shopkeeper.

manas.q: Name a CBC value about telling the truth.

children.note: Being someone others can rely on, and trusting others fairly. Example: a child trusted to carry the family's shopping money.
Choosing what is right even when no one is watching. Example: not copying a friend's work in class.
KICD has values-based education materials and reported plans for a nationwide rollout by 2026. Ask your school how it is used.
In Grade 10–12 learners choose a pathway (a broad area) and, within it, a track (a group of subjects). This is an outline; see the Senior school map for detail.
KICD's course book lists show three pathways: STEM, Social Sciences, and Arts and Sports Science.

manas.q: What are the three senior school pathways?

children.note: Science, technology, engineering and maths.
Includes Biology, Chemistry, Physics, General Science and Mathematics.
Includes Agriculture, Computer Studies, Home Science and ICT.
Includes Building Construction, Electricity, Woodwork, Power Mechanics, Aviation and more.
Languages, people and society.
Includes English, Literature in English, Kiswahili, Fasihi ya Kiswahili and foreign languages.
Includes CRE, IRE, History & Citizenship, Geography, Business Studies and Community Service Learning.
For learners drawn to the arts or sport.
Includes Music and Dance, Theatre and Film, and Fine Arts.
Includes Sports and Recreation, and Physical Education.
The lists we read do not show which subjects every learner must take or how many. Check with your school or the Ministry's current guidance.
CBC aims to balance everyday classroom checks with assessments at the end of some levels.
Teachers watch, ask questions and check work during lessons to see what each child can do and what help they need next.

manas.q: What is formative assessment, in plain words?

children.note: Some assessments come at the end of a stage. The framework wants these balanced with classroom checks, not replacing them.
Projects, oral work, practical tasks, observation and written work can all show learning, not only a written test.
A portfolio is a collection of a child's work over time. KICD's parent guidelines mention portfolios and learners' diaries as records.

manas.q: What is a learner's portfolio?

children.note: Read your child's report card and teacher comments, then respond and agree a plan with the teacher.
National assessments come at the end of Grade 3, Grade 6 and Grade 9. Check the current names and timing with your school or KNEC.

manas.q: Which body runs national assessments in Kenya?

children.note: Learning by helping the community, then talking about what was learnt. It links classroom knowledge to real needs.
Learners use their knowledge and skills on a real community need, planned with community partners, then reflect on it in class.

manas.q: What is community service learning?

children.note: Projects can tackle human, safety, educational or environmental needs, such as a clean-up or a tree-planting day.
KICD's parent guidelines say activities should be safe and suit the child's age.
Cleaning the school, for example, is meant as a learning activity, never as a punishment.
In senior school, Community Service Learning also appears as a subject in the Social Sciences pathway lists.
CBC asks parents to be active partners. KICD's guidelines call this Parental Empowerment and Engagement.
Empowerment = helping parents gain the know-how to support children. Engagement = parents taking an active part with teachers.

manas.q: What two words make up 'PE&E' in CBC?

children.note: Everyday ways to support learning at home.
Show interest and help find materials, but let the child do the work.
Children copy what they see; values are 'caught rather than taught'.
Age-right play and chores build body, mind and character. Example: sorting beans, sweeping, counting change.
Notice what your child loves and where they struggle, then talk to the teacher early.

children.topic: Quality time and a safe home
children.note: Talking, reading and a calm, safe space to learn matter more than costly items.
Ways to take part in school life.
Go to parent meetings, academic clinics, sports days and music and drama festivals.
Take part in the Parents' Association and the school Board of Management: attend, vote, share ideas.
A tailor, farmer or mechanic parent can share skills with learners when the school asks.
Keep communication regular and two-way: school diary, phone, SMS or class WhatsApp group.
Signed diaries help teachers know messages reached home.
Agree with the teacher on clear steps to help your child improve.
Use what is around you: market trips for maths, a kitchen garden for science, stories from grandparents for language and culture.
Several bodies share the work. This is what we could confirm.
The Kenya Institute of Curriculum Development (set up by Act No. 4 of 2013) develops CBC designs and approves course books.

manas.q: Which body designs the CBC curriculum?

children.note: The Kenya National Examinations Council oversees national exams and assessments and issues certificates.
The Teachers Service Commission registers and employs teachers for public schools, and posts, promotes and disciplines them.

manas.q: Which body employs public school teachers in Kenya?

children.note: Schools and teachers turn the curriculum designs into daily lessons and classroom assessment.
The Ministry leads education policy. KICD's parent guidelines were issued for the Ministry.
Parents share responsibility for learning and values, through home support, the PA and the BoM.
